text:
sara: noticed via SIEM alert — several backup-agent multipart uploads to s3://redwood-backups/staging/ showed no SSE headers. maybe during last KMS key rotation window.

aj: omg. timestamp? how many objects?

sara: spotted at 2026-03-20T18:02Z. about ~1200 chunk objects (multipart parts) across 3 prefixes. head-object shows no ServerSideEncryption header.

dan: can you paste one head-object call?

sara: ```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-backups --key staging/part-00012
# Response headers: Content-Length, ETag, but no ServerSideEncryption
```

linda: backup-agent uploads multipart parts without SSE if the uploader role temporarily loses kms:Encrypt permission. We rotated grants earlier today for the backup-sa.

aj: timeline: we applied key policy change at 17:58Z and ran grant prune script at 17:59Z. ops-oncall — did we redeploy backup agent around then?

ops-oncall: yes, 18:00Z we bumped agent to v3.4.2 with new env var. might have re-auth handshake.

sara: hypothesis: agent retried in middle of grant window and parts landed without SSE header. S3 accepts parts without SSE if the client doesn't set it.

dan: severity? data exfil risk? were any of the objects made public or replicated?

linda: buckets are private. no public ACLs. but snapshot tooling replicates to cold-archive (different account) later in lifecycle.

aj: immediate mitigations: 1) Pause backup-agent rollout 2) Add S3 bucket-level default encryption 3) Revoke any temporary public grants 4) Inventory non-encrypted objects

sara: already paused agent rollout. filing change to add default encryption now (IAM required). running inventory script: ```
# simple inventory
aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-backups --prefix staging/ --query 'Contents[].Key' | xargs -n1 -I{} aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-backups --key {} --output json | jq '.Key, .ServerSideEncryption' 
```

ops-oncall: nice. if ServerSideEncryption is null we need to re-encrypt via copy with SSE-KMS. Example:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/staging/part-00012 /tmp/part && aws s3 cp /tmp/part s3://redwood-backups/staging/part-00012 --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:key/REDACTED
```

linda: copying locally will be slow. better: S3 copy-object from same bucket to same key with metadata-directive REPLACE and --sse

dan: runbook update: add step to check KMS grants before rotation; do a smoke upload that verifies SSE headers on head-object. Add permission check to rotation playbook.

aj: RBAC fix: ensure backup-sa has a short-lived sts assume role with kms:Encrypt + kms:GenerateDataKey permissions and add a condition 'aws:CalledVia' to block accidental tokenless uploads.

sara: audit logging: we need to search CloudTrail for PutObject/UploadPart events without SSE info. query: ```
fields @timestamp, eventName, requestParameters.bucketName, requestParameters.key, userIdentity.principalId
| filter eventName in ['PutObject','UploadPart']
| filter requestParameters.headers.ServerSideEncryption = null
```

ops-oncall: also check S3 access logs and the backup-agent logs for 'No SSE' warnings. Forward findings to SIEM and open an incident ticket.

linda: for recovery: identify affected manifests and mark snapshots as 're-encrypt required' so cold-archive won't pick them up. We'll block cross-account replication for those prefixes until re-encrypt job finishes.

aj: longer-term: add CI smoke that performs multipart upload under rotation scenarios and asserts head-object SSE header. Also add unit test in grant-prune to ensure no gap during key policy flips.

sara: who will own remediation? volunteer list?

linda: I'll own object re-encrypt job (s3 CopyObject with metadata replace) and coordinate with dan for throttling.

dan: I'll update runbooks and put RBAC guardrails in terraform change.

aj: I'll add audit queries + SIEM dashboards and a postmortem template entries about KMS rotation blast radius.

ops-oncall: reassigning incident P0 -> sec-encops. Recommend communicating to customers if any tenant snapshots may be impacted (data was not public but re-encrypt pending).

sara: I'll draft a brief external blurb. keep it factual: "we detected temporary lack of at-rest encryption for parts of staging snapshots during key rotation; no public exposure detected; remediation in progress."

aj: good. after re-encrypt, run integrity check against manifests and close incident. add a retro to adjust rotation window.

encops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0332 severity P0, owners: linda, aj, dan, sara

sara: thanks team. will post updates here as we progress.
